interpretation: Two fresh-rootfs read-only runs preserve every prior field, constructor, writer, JNI, JSON-prefix, SHA-256 and AES observation for the fixed 49-character/frame-type-0 profile. The +0x268584 -> +0x2481fc constructor copies 93 bytes; its object and contents match the actual AES data operand. Copy callback 24 moves 88 bytes from final-buffer offset 0 to offset 1 with overlap. Callback 25 copies a separate stable four-byte source to offset 89. Both callbacks return at the saved dispatcher SP and their destination bytes equal their saved source snapshots and final AES slices. The final first byte is written by VM STRB +0x171c18. Before copy 12 scratch fill, the observed 88-byte buffer has within-run A-B-A-B states that differ only at offset 0; later the final AES plaintext differs across all of [0,89), with a common four-byte suffix. This narrows the observed difference boundary, without identifying the origin of that first byte or proving causality by intervention. The buffer receives 176 observed VM byte writes: 88 at bytecode location +0xa0f08 and 11 at each of eight bytecode locations +0xa0e7c through +0xa0ea4. Their first/last sequence numbers show interleaving, not two whole-buffer passes. The intermediate snapshot is specifically before the FIRST +0xa0e7c buffer store, when only [0,8) differs from the pre-block snapshot; it must not be treated as an intermediate state of all eleven blocks. The earlier stages probes interpreted individual +0xa0f08 store operands as a final whole-buffer output; later block stores overwrite them, so those failed comparisons do not refute the store operands or identify an algorithm. No raw operands, first-byte values, keys, IVs, signatures, operand digests or character masks are published. Pre-block first-byte origin, block transform, suffix generation, key/IV generation, alternation root cause, other inputs, Android equality, independent signer and online acceptance remain unverified.
